title: Stalls
summary: General stalling workflow for idle stalls, decel stalls, hot stalls, starts-then-dies, and intermittent shutdowns.
intro: A stalling complaint should be tied to the condition where it happens: hot restart, idle in gear, decel, bumps, fuel level, A/C load, or highway cruise. Testing should capture what drops out first: RPM signal, fuel pressure, spark, throttle/idle control, power feed, or communication.
common_sounds: Engine shuts off at stop lights
Stalls when hot and restarts after cooling
Stalls when turning on A/C or shifting into gear
Stalls over bumps or during deceleration
quick_checks: Scan all modules and save freeze-frame data for stall-related codes
Monitor RPM signal, fuel pressure, throttle angle, idle command, battery voltage, and MAF/MAP data during the stall
Inspect battery terminals, engine grounds, PCM power relay, and harness areas disturbed by engine movement
Check throttle body cleanliness, idle relearn needs, vacuum leaks, and purge valve leakage for idle stalls
Use heat, vibration, and wiggle testing only after a safe baseline inspection
common_causes: Crankshaft position sensor or RPM signal dropout
Fuel pump pressure loss, relay issue, or restricted fuel delivery
Dirty throttle body, idle control issue, or vacuum leak
EVAP purge valve stuck open causing rich idle or starts-then-stalls
Poor power, ground, relay, or intermittent connector fault
MAF/MAP signal error or engine mechanical issue

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Dropout Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Find whether RPM, spark, fuel, PCM power, or communication disappears first.
checks: Check fuel pressure during the stall

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Idle Air and Load Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: For stalls at stops or with A/C load, inspect airflow, throttle, purge, and vacuum leak behavior.
checks: Check purge valve sealing at idle
Smoke test intake and PCV leak paths

recommended_repairs.title: Fuel Pump Replacement
